units.title: 3.1 Unseen translation, comprehension, pointing and composition

outcomes.text: Widen vocabulary and structures by reading extra passages of Biblical Hebrew beyond the set texts.
Recognise, explain and use the listed accidence and syntax in unseen passages.
Translate unseen prose and poetry accurately into English.
Show detailed understanding of words, phrases, clauses and sentences in the original.
Answer comprehension, syntax and accidence questions on unseen prose and poetry.
Add vowel pointing to about two lines of unpointed narrative prose.
Translate English passages into pointed Biblical Hebrew.
Present information clearly in English using proper grammatical terms.
Appreciate Biblical Hebrew literature and its techniques with a critical eye.
Study two prose and two poetry set texts in detail.
Read ancient literature in English translation to understand each set text's literary context.
Understand the social, cultural and historical backgrounds of the set texts.
Use historical or cultural knowledge to explain a phrase, clause or passage.
Identify, analyse and evaluate literary techniques, characterisation, argument and meaning in set texts.
Name literary features using appropriate English technical terms.
Choose relevant evidence from the texts to support an argument and summarise findings.
Write clear, coherent extended answers on passages and topics, including translated material.
Translate passages of each set text into English and respond to passages.
Develop independent judgement about the texts and their contexts.
Explain more complex grammatical forms where they occur in the set texts.
Give up to two explanations of a difficult or ambiguous word, justified by context or grammar.
Trace the derivation of nouns from verbal forms and of personal and place names.
Know background on incidents, characters, places and people needed to follow the story.
Locate important places approximately on maps of the region.
Give gender, number and state of regular and irregular nouns.
Form nouns using the preformative letters mem, aleph, tav and the afformative nun.
Make adjectives agree with their nouns.
Form comparatives and superlatives of adjectives.
Use cardinal and ordinal numbers.
Attach pronominal suffixes to nouns, verbs and prepositions.
Recognise weaknesses in verb roots.
Conjugate all persons and numbers of perfect, imperfect and imperative.
Form and use the cohortative, jussive and polite imperative.
Use participles in every conjugation as verbs, nouns or adjectives, including the qal passive participle.
Form and explain the function of qal, niphal, piel, hiphil and hithpael.
Handle contracted and irregular verbs: pe-yod, pe-nun, ayin-vav, lamed-he, pe and ayin guttural, geminate, and hithpael first-letter changes.
Recognise common hophal and pual forms.
Recognise common polel, hithpolel, pilpel and hithpalpel forms.
Form and use the infinitive construct.
Form and use the infinitive absolute.
Use inseparable prepositions and the preposition meaning 'from'.
Use the definite article.
Use the interrogative he.
Use vav conjunctive.
Use vav conversive (consecutive).
Form and recognise the gentilic yod.
Use the locative he.
Recognise paragogic letters.
Identify syllables and vowels, including sheva and hataf vowels.
Distinguish weak, strong and euphonic dagesh.
Explain how guttural and labial letters affect pointing.
Explain how milra and milei accents affect pointing.
Recognise and form pausal forms.
Describe Hebrew word order.
Translate relative, oath and interrogative clauses.
Translate common conditional sentences.
Translate temporal, concessive and causal clauses.
Translate purpose and result clauses.
Translate verbless and asseverative clauses.
Translate common negative clauses, including legal prohibitions.
Recognise and correctly use the examinable grammatical terms and accepted alternatives.
Use noun terms: construct form, preformative, cardinal, ordinal, dual, mappiq, pronominal suffix, singular, plural, comparative, superlative.
Use verb terms: root, aspect, geminate, root-letter names, perfect, imperfect, cohortative, jussive, imperatives, infinitives, negative mem.
Use stem terms: binyan, qal, niphal, piel, hiphil, hithpael, pual, hophal, active, passive, causative, reflexive, interactive, participle.

subtopics.title: Terms for morphemes, pointing and syntax

outcomes.text: Use morpheme terms: definite article, interrogative he, locative he, vav conjunctive, vav consecutive, gentilic yod.
Name vowel signs, sheva types, syllable types, guttural and labial letters, and dagesh types.
Use syntax terms: parallelism, pausal form, subject, object, ellipsis.
Study the four set texts and the additional English reading.
Know that the set texts stay valid for the life of the specification.
Study I Samuel 1-7 (omitting 2:1-10) in Hebrew.
Study II Kings 9-13 in Hebrew, with listed English background readings from I and II Kings.
Study Jeremiah 13-18 in Hebrew.
Study Psalms 50-59 in Hebrew, with listed English readings from I and II Samuel.
Build on the Core Vocabulary List through wide reading; no defined list is set.
Know the general core vocabulary, including verbs from listed roots and numbers.
